kept.claim: The new Javadoc for requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says it throws when canManageMembership() is false, but the implementation checks canManageMembers(), which has different semantics (managing member users vs adding users to the group).
kept.body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] `requireManageMembers` Javadoc references the wrong check

**Severity:** LOW -- the documented contract is wrong for a security check

### The Problem

```java
/**
 * Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}.
 */
void requireManageMembers(GroupModel group);
```

The implementation in `GroupPermissions.requireManageMembers` (line ~376) calls `canManageMembers(group)`. The Javadoc links to the wrong method.

### Theory / Proof

The two scopes mean different things in this PR. `manage-members` lets the admin manage the users who belong to the group (`canManage(UserModel)` uses it through `canManageByGroup`). `manage-membership` lets the admin add or remove users from the group. `UsersResource.createUser` (line ~195) calls both `requireManageMembers` and `requireManageMembership` because they are distinct. A reader who trusts this Javadoc will conclude that one call is redundant.

### What happens today vs. what will break

Runtime behaviour is correct today. The risk is that someone later "simplifies" `createUser`, or writes a new implementation, based on the documented contract.

### Research

Every other `require*` Javadoc added in this PR links to its own `can*` counterpart.

### Recommendation

```java
/**
 * Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembers(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}.
 */
void requireManageMembers(GroupModel group);
```
kept.evidence: The Javadoc says canManageMembership, but GroupPermissions.java:376-380 checks canManageMembers. These are distinct checks (GroupPermissionsV2.java:90-103), and UsersResource.java:195-196 calls both. Documentation only; runtime unaffected.
